title: AppTest - add support for st.image and st.download_button
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Requesting st.image and st.download_button to be added to AppTest

### Why?

Images and download buttons are key features of our streamlit app, and we'd like to use AppTest to write automated tests for these widgets.

### How?

New properties within AppTest class for getting sequences of all st.image and st.download_button widgets.

### Additional Context

_No response_

Would still be good to eventually be able to use AppTest's more advanced interaction-simulation at some point.

> As a workaround, I think you should be able to do something like `at.get("imgs")` or `at.get("download_button")`

Is it possible to click the download button and receive the file from `at.get("download_button")` ?

The following workaround works for me for a case where there is only one download_button.

```python
import streamlit as st

class DownloadButton(object): # Singleton (only be created once) class to hold inputs to download button
    def __new__(cls, label=None, data=None, file_name=None, mime=None):
        # Note: I only set this up to handle inputs that I'm using but it can obviously be extended
        if not hasattr(cls, 'instance'):
            cls.instance = super(DownloadButton, cls).__new__(cls) # Create singleton if it does not exist
            cls.instance.value = False

        cls.instance.label = label
        cls.instance.data = data
        cls.instance.file_name = file_name
        cls.instance.mime = mime

        return cls.instance
    
    def click(self):
        self.value = True
  

def download_button(label, data, file_name, mime):
    btn = DownloadButton(label, data, file_name, mime)

    out = btn.value
    if out and callable(btn.data):
        btn.data = data()
    btn.value = False  # Set to False to revert value after a button click
    return out

def columns(ncols, *args, **kwargs):  # Extend st.columns to include download button function
    all_cols = st._main.columns(ncols, *args, **kwargs)
    for c in all_cols:
        c.download_button = download_button

    return all_cols

# Replace streamlit functions
st.download_button = download_button
st.columns = columns

def test_download(app):    
    btn = DownloadButton()
    btn.click()
    app.run()

    assert isinstance(btn.data, bytes)
```
